ns2:section.sectionText: Description: History 251 addresses the history of warfare and military institutions during the last two hundred years. Subjects covered include the impact of the Industrial Revolution on military technology and practice, the influence of military theory (including the work of Clausewitz), the development of staffs and doctrine, the phenomenon of total war, the character of insurgency, and the rise of global terrorism. Conflicts studied in some detail include the U.S. Civil War, World War I, World War II, the Korean War, the Vietnam War, the Arab-Israeli Wars, and the "war" on terrorism. The material presented is specifically designed to interest a wide range of students who simply want to know more about history of armed conflict. Learn more about this inescapable, though regrettable, side of human experience.
